label: Mould and damp
summary: Mould grows in any building that has been wet for a few days. Its spores irritate the nose, eyes and lungs, set off asthma, and can cause serious lung infections in people who are already ill, very old, or have weak immune systems. Wet buildings also hide rotten floors.
signs: Black, green, grey or white fuzzy or slimy patches
Water stains, peeling paint, and swollen wood or plasterboard
Soggy carpets, cardboard, ceiling tiles and insulation
do: Open up and air out a damp space before working in it
Wear a mask and goggles in mouldy rooms
Dampen mouldy material lightly before moving it, to keep spores down
Bag mouldy items and take them outside
Keep shelter spaces dry and fix leaks quickly
dont: Don't bring mouldy bedding, clothes or cardboard into your shelter
Don't mix bleach with ammonia or acid cleaners
Don't let people with asthma, allergies, lung disease or a weak immune system do mould clean-up
ppe: An N95 or P2 mask or better
firstAid: Coughing, wheezing or sore eyes: get to fresh air and rinse eyes with clean water
Use the person's own reliever inhaler if they have one; if it doesn't help or they can't speak in full sentences, it's an emergency: keep them sitting up and get help
A cough that won't go, fever, chest pain or coughing blood needs medical care, especially for the old, the ill or the pregnant
